newsitem.title: INDIA: Enron says India unit to start in Dec 1998.
newsitem.headline: Enron says India unit to start in Dec 1998.

text.p: U.S. energy giant Enron Corp said on Wednesday it expected to complete the first phase of its controversial Indian power project by December 1998, ahead of an earlier target date of March 1999.

Work on the 2,450 MW power plant in India's western Maharashtra state resumed late last year after the ruling Hindu nationalist government renegotiated a contract it had said was too expensive in terms of project and tariffs.

"The first phase of the project will be completed three months ahead of the renegotiated schedule," Kenneth Lay, chairman and chief executive officer of Enron, told a news conference jointly addressed by state officials.
"The project is environmentally sound and the cleanest," Lay added.
The first phase of the $2.3-billion-project will generate 740 MW of electricity, Maharashtra's deputy chief minister Gopinath Munde said.
"Accordingly, tenders have been issued before work begins on a 75-km transmission line from the project site," Munde added.
Munde said the negotiations for the Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) on the project's 1440 MW second phase would begin by February 25, and be completed by the end of 1997.
"Work on the second phase will begin in 1998," Lay added.
The project will use natural gas for power generation, he said.

Enron's Dabhol Power Company, the firm's local arm, was one of eight fast track projects designed to lure foreign private investment into India's crumbling infrastructure sector shortly after open market reforms were launched in 1991.

Work was delayed for over a year because of a political tug-of-war between the Congress government which negotiated the contract, and the Hindu nationalist coalition which defeated it in local polls in March 1995.
It resumed late last year, after the terms of the deal were renegotiated.
